note: Ground-truth labels for the RecoveryCall QA dataset. 'split' is 'dev' (original dev set; rules v1 were built on it), 'dev_v2' (held-out v1, spent after one evaluation on 2026-10-21 and merged into development; see docs/baseline_rules_v1.md), 'held_out' (held-out v2: written externally, labels checked by reading before any classifier ran; evaluated once on text and now spent, docs/held_out_v2_results.md) or 'held_out_v3' (held-out v3: written externally, labels checked by reading before any audio was made; end-to-end audio evaluation only). Labels follow the definition in prepare_labels.py (held_out is held-out v2, added 2026-10-21): telling/showing family, employer, neighbours or contacts = third_party_contact_threat; visiting/harming/shaming in person = intimidation_or_threats; multi-label allowed. 'compliant' is false when the call contains a conduct concern or a threatening authority claim. 'concern_types' lists the categories present. 'authority_mention' is true when the agent mentions police, arrest, FIR, court or a legal notice (including lawful mentions in compliant calls); it is scored as a verify flag, separately from the three conduct categories. 'concern_spans' quote the labelled text (turn index + exact substring); dev entries carry authority spans only. 'hard_negative' is true only for compliant calls containing firm-but-lawful language that must not be flagged. 'needs_native_review' is true for Kannada scripts pending native speaker review. 'label_changes' logs every change from the delivered labels.

concern_type_labels.intimidation_or_threats: Physical threats, agents visiting, sending men to debtor's location
concern_type_labels.abusive_language: Slurs, derogatory or shaming language directed at the debtor
concern_type_labels.third_party_contact_threat: Threatening to contact family, employer, neighbours, or other third parties
concern_type_labels.authority_or_legal_action_claim: Claiming police, arrest, court summons, or official legal process
